s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological decline with bulbar and cognitive involvement
key_facts: 6-month history of progressive symptoms
Family history of memory problems after age 80
Cognitive impairment on neurological examination
Vertical gaze palsy on neurological examination
Tongue atrophy on neurological examination
Pyramidal signs on neurological examination
Severe loss of dopamine transporter binding in basal ganglia on 11C-CFT PET imaging
Almost total loss of dopamine transporter binding in caudate nucleus on 11C-CFT PET imaging
Abnormal needle EMG findings in frontalis, mentalis, orbicularis oculi, and genioglossus muscles
Heterozygous pathogenic variant of TBK1 gene identified by whole-exon sequencing
Autoimmune encephalitis antibodies negative in serum and CSF

shortlist.label: TBK1-associated frontotemporal dementia
shortlist.why_kept: Heterozygous pathogenic variant of TBK1 gene identified by whole-exon sequencing

shortlist.label: Frontotemporal dementia
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive neurological decline with cognitive impairment and bulbar involvement

shortlist.label: Progressive supranuclear palsy
shortlist.why_kept: Vertical gaze palsy and severe loss of dopamine transporter binding in basal ganglia

shortlist.label: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Tongue atrophy and abnormal needle EMG findings in bulbar muscles

shortlist.label: Corticobasal degeneration
shortlist.why_kept: Pyramidal signs and cognitive impairment with asymmetric motor features

raw.rationale: The presence of a heterozygous pathogenic variant of the TBK1 gene, along with the combination of cognitive impairment, vertical gaze palsy, tongue atrophy, pyramidal signs, and severe loss of dopamine transporter binding in basal ganglia, supports this diagnosis

rejected.label: Frontotemporal dementia
rejected.why: While cognitive impairment is present, the specific genetic finding and constellation of other symptoms point more specifically to TBK1-associated frontotemporal dementia

rejected.label: Progressive supranuclear palsy
rejected.why: Vertical gaze palsy is consistent with this diagnosis, but the genetic finding and other symptoms do not fully align

rejected.label: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
rejected.why: Tongue atrophy and abnormal needle EMG findings could suggest ALS, but the presence of cognitive impairment and vertical gaze palsy, along with the genetic finding, do not support this as the primary diagnosis

rejected.label: Corticobasal degeneration
rejected.why: While some symptoms could overlap, the specific combination of findings, including the genetic result, does not align closely with corticobasal degeneration
